Statement: LabWare handles two main filetypes – inbound OIS requests and instrument data files. The mechanism for receiving these is the same – Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP). This is not a native LabWare function. Instead, windows shell scripts are executed by a LabWare background instance. The location of these scripts and the file structure of the server differs, by application.
Each script comes in 2 parts – a .bat and a .txt file.
Analyses are assigned to samples based on a combination of test media and requested analyte codes. These relationships are stored in the Occupational Chemical Database (OCD).

In order for tests to be assigned, the inbound sample must have a matching record on the X_OCD_MONITORING table for Analyte Code and Media, and the analysis must have an Analysis Variation with the corresponding method assigned.
Originally a document stored on the DOL Intranet, the OCD has been parsed into four tables in LabWare:
Holds the name of the material groups that there are testing standards for, as well as associated hazard information
Acts as a parent table for the remaining OCD tables
Creates the link between the X_ANALYTE_CODE table and the X_OCD_STANDARD table
Contains testing methods for analyte codes based on sample media
Contains the physical properties of a standard
Lists the literature reference based on source for a standard

Alternatively called “substance codes” or “IMIS codes,” these are unique identifiers that pair standards to test methods. Each standard may have multiple analyte codes, but each analyte code is under only one standard. The primary key for analyte codes is a 4-character alphanumeric string stored on the X_ANALYTE_CODE table.
There are three distinct categories of sample: Air, Wipe, and Bulk. These correspond to different entries in the Monitoring Methods table

Analysis Limits do not get checked inherently. You may set them up in the Analysis Limits table but will have to apply them during result calculations. See CALC_ICP_FINAL for an example where the Analysis Limits table is referenced and used to set a reporting limit.

Every raw instrument result has a corresponding Lower Reporting Limit that is set based on measured Reporting Limit Spiked Media samples annually in a separate process. That reporting limit, stored on the Analysis Limits table (ANALYSIS_LIMITS.MIN_LIMIT) should be used to generate a reporting limit on all final results and stored in the RESULT.X_REPORTING_LIMIT field. Generally, all actions that are performed on the raw result to transform it to the final result should be carried out on the Lower Reporting Limit value in parallel. A format calculation (in most cases, the calc ICP_LOWER_LIMIT is used) will check the RESULT.ENTRY value against the RESULT.X_REPORTING_LIMIT value for a final result and, if necessary, act as a lower bracket (reporting “<RL” in the case the final value is too low to be reported).

Recovery results are used for Standards, Controls, QCSMs, and RLSMs. They represent the fraction of analyte measured against the theoretical content. Example: If a sample is known to have 100mg analyte A on it and testing returns 99mg, the sample has 0.99 recovery. This ratio is unitless.

For Empower peak components, the data type should be set to “Text” even though the result is a number. This is because when Empower does not detect a peak through its processing method, it returns the string “ND” instead of the number “0.” The resultant data type mismatch will trigger a runtime error.

Typically, a Batch Template is intended to work for only one analytical method. Some analytical methods, however, are considered compatible and may be tested together. In this case, ensure that the ANALYSIS_METHODS table correctly pairs methods with a variation on the analysis and that variation has the “parent” method set. Additionally, on the T_ANALYSIS_METHOD table, the X_RELATED_METHOD field must be set to point from the child method to the parent method that matches the Analysis Variation method. Note that the ANALYSIS_METHOD table is a child table of ANALYSIS and the T_ANALYSIS_METHOD table is its own separate table. The ANALYSIS -> ANALYSIS_METHOD table is used to pair method with variation, while the T_ANALYSIS_METHOD holds the master data related to methods.
In Gas Chromatography (Analysis: GC), method OSHA_111 may be tested using the OSHA_5000_PASSIVE variation. The methods and analyses are configured:

Analysis Method -> Method = OSHA_111, Variation = OSHA_5000_PASSIVE
T_ANALYSIS_METHOD (OSHA_111) -> X Related Method = OSHA_5000

Each batch uses a Batch Standard Protocol to automatically add standard sets to the batch. These standards are configured on the QC_SAMPLES table. Typically, a batch standard protocol includes a calibration blank (CB), several standards (STD_A, STD_B, etc), and an initial calibration verification control (ICV). Additionally, one or more continuing calibration verification  control (CCV) samples may be used.

Statement: CCVs are special cases for the OSHA batch analysis. Typically these control samples are run several times in the batch process, once for every 10 field samples tested. Due to the uncertain nature or variable nature of CCVs, it is necessary to treat these samples dynamically.
